say.en: Milk that keeps for a week in the fridge goes sour in a day on the kitchen shelf. A small rise in temperature can make reactions much faster. In this lesson: State the Arrhenius equation and explain activation energy.
Calculate Ea from rate constants at two temperatures.

title.en: Activation energy and the Arrhenius equation

body.en: For many reactions the rate constant nearly doubles for a 10 K rise. Arrhenius explained this: reactants must pass over an energy barrier, the *activation energy* Ea, through an unstable activated complex. The fraction of molecules with energy ≥ Ea is e^(−Ea/RT), and this fraction grows sharply with temperature (the Maxwell–Boltzmann curve flattens and shifts right). A is the frequency (pre-exponential) factor.
body.kn: ಕ್ರಿಯಾಕಾರಿಗಳು ಸಕ್ರಿಯಗೊಳಿಸುವ ಶಕ್ತಿ Ea ಎಂಬ ಶಕ್ತಿ ತಡೆಗೋಡೆಯನ್ನು ದಾಟಬೇಕು. Ea ಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ಅಣುಗಳ ಭಾಗ e^(−Ea/RT); ತಾಪಮಾನ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದಂತೆ ಈ ಭಾಗ ತೀವ್ರವಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: For many reactions the rate constant nearly doubles for a 10 kelvin rise. Arrhenius explained this: reactants must pass over an energy barrier, the activation energy Ea, through an unstable activated complex. The fraction of molecules with energy is greater than or equal to Ea is e^(-Ea over RT), and this fraction grows sharply with temperature (the Maxwell-Boltzmann curve flattens and shifts right). A is the frequency (pre-exponential) factor. k equals A e^(-Ea over RT).
say.kn: ಕ್ರಿಯಾಕಾರಿಗಳು ಸಕ್ರಿಯಗೊಳಿಸುವ ಶಕ್ತಿ Ea ಎಂಬ ಶಕ್ತಿ ತಡೆಗೋಡೆಯನ್ನು ದಾಟಬೇಕು. Ea ಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ಅಣುಗಳ ಭಾಗ e^(-Ea over RT); ತಾಪಮಾನ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದಂತೆ ಈ ಭಾಗ ತೀವ್ರವಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: the Arrhenius equation

say.en: Reactants must climb an energy barrier, the activation energy, to reach the activated complex before they fall to products.
Arrhenius: k equals A times e to the minus E a over R T. A higher temperature or a lower barrier gives a larger k.
Take natural logs: ln k against 1 over T is a straight line with slope minus E a over R.
Comparing two temperatures removes A.
Example: the rate doubles from 300 to 310 kelvin. Then E a works out to about 53.6 kilojoules per mole.

text.en: Rate doubles from 300 K to 310 K

say.en: Why so sensitive? At a higher temperature the energy curve spreads out, and the fraction beyond E a, the tail, grows a lot.
On the board: the Arrhenius equation.

narration.en: The curve shows how molecular energies are spread at temperature T. Only collisions with energy above Ea react; that fraction is about e^(−Ea/RT). A small rise in T fattens the tail a lot, so k = A e^(−Ea/RT) grows quickly.
narration.kn: ವಕ್ರ T ತಾಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಅಣು ಶಕ್ತಿಗಳ ಹರಡುವಿಕೆ ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. Ea ಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಶಕ್ತಿಯ ಘರ್ಷಣೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಕ್ರಿಯಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಆ ಭಾಗ ಸುಮಾರು e^(−Ea/RT). ತಾಪ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಏರಿದರೂ k = A e^(−Ea/RT) ವೇಗವಾಗಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Writing the Arrhenius equation at T₁ and T₂ and subtracting removes A: $\log\frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{E_a}{2.303R}\left(\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1T_2}\right)$. Measure k at two *temperatures* and you can find Ea; know Ea and you can predict k at a new temperature.
body.kn: ಎರಡು ತಾಪಮಾನಗಳಲ್ಲಿ k ಅಳೆದು Ea ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಬಹುದು: log(k₂/k₁) = (Ea/2.303R)(T₂ − T₁)/(T₁T₂).

points.en: Use R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ and T in kelvin

narration.en: Write the Arrhenius equation at two temperatures and subtract: log of k2 by k1 equals Ea by 2.303 R, times T2 minus T1 over T1 T2. Measure k at two temperatures and you can find the activation energy.
narration.kn: ಎರಡು ತಾಪಮಾನಗಳಲ್ಲಿ k ಅಳೆದು Ea ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಬಹುದು: log(k₂/k₁) = (Ea/2.303R)(T₂ − T₁)/(T₁T₂).

say.en: Write the Arrhenius equation at two temperatures and subtract: log of k2 by k1 equals Ea by 2.303 R, times T2 minus T1 over T1 T2. Measure k at two temperatures and you can find the activation energy. Use R equals 8.314 joules K to the power minus 1 mol to the power minus 1 and T in kelvin.
say.kn: ಎರಡು ತಾಪಮಾನಗಳಲ್ಲಿ k ಅಳೆದು Ea ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಬಹುದು: log(k 2 over k 1) equals (Ea over 2.303R)(T 2 - T 1)/T 1T 2.

problem.en: The rate constant of a reaction doubles when the temperature rises from 300 K to 310 K. Find Ea.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. The rate constant of a reaction doubles when the temperature rises from 300 K to 310 K. Find Ea.

say.en: Let us solve this together. The rate constant of a reaction doubles when the temperature rises from 300 kelvin to 310 kelvin. Find Ea.
log 2 equals (Ea over 2.303R) times 310 minus 300/300 times 310.
0.3010 equals Ea times 10 over (2.303 times 8.314 times 93 000).
Ea equals 0.3010 times 2.303 times 8.314 times 9300 equals 53 600 joules mol to the power minus 1.
So the answer is Ea is approximately 53.6 kilojoules mol to the power minus 1.

problem.en: A reaction has a temperature coefficient of 2. By what factor does its rate increase from 25 °C to 65 °C?

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A reaction has a temperature coefficient of 2. By what factor does its rate increase from 25 °C to 65 °C?

say.en: Let us solve this together. A reaction has a temperature coefficient of 2. By what factor does its rate increase from 25 degrees Celsius to 65 degrees Celsius?
Rise equals 40 degrees Celsius equals 4 steps of 10 degrees Celsius.
Factor equals 2 to the power 4 equals 16.
So the answer is 16 times.

narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. k = A e^(−Ea/RT); ತಾಪಮಾನ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದರೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಅಣುಗಳು ತಡೆಗೋಡೆ ದಾಟುತ್ತವೆ. ln k ಮತ್ತು 1/T ನಕ್ಷೆಯ ಇಳಿಜಾರು −Ea/R. log(k₂/k₁) = (Ea/2.303R)(T₂ − T₁)/(T₁T₂).

say.en: Let us recall the key ideas. k equals A e^(-Ea over RT); higher temperature, more molecules cross the barrier.
say.kn: ಮುಖ್ಯ ಅಂಶಗಳನ್ನು ನೆನಪಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. k equals A e^(-Ea over RT); ತಾಪಮಾನ ಹೆಚ್ಚಿದರೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಅಣುಗಳು ತಡೆಗೋಡೆ ದಾಟುತ್ತವೆ.

say.en: ln k vs 1 over T is a straight line of slope -Ea over R.
say.kn: ln k ಮತ್ತು 1 over T ನಕ್ಷೆಯ ಇಳಿಜಾರು -Ea over R.

say.en: log(k 2 over k 1) equals (Ea over 2.303R)(T 2 - T 1)/T 1T 2.
say.kn: log(k 2 over k 1) equals (Ea over 2.303R)(T 2 - T 1)/T 1T 2.

say.en: Next: Catalysts and collision theory.
